Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
1231 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
A Wind Advisory has been issued for much of the area. The High 
Wind Watch and Storm Watch remain in effect and unchanged.

A Coastal Flood Watch issued for the entire coastline except 
for southeast CT for Thanksgiving through the daytime high tide 
cycle on Friday. A Coastal Flood Advisory issued for southeast 
CT for this same timeframe.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) A storm system impacts the area Thanksgiving into Friday 
with rain and strong to damaging winds.

2) Widespread moderate coastal flooding likely for the 
Thanksgiving AM and PM high tides, with minor to moderate 
impacts for the Friday AM high tide. In addition, widespread 
beach flooding and dune erosion expected along the open water 
shorelines during the times of high tide, with localized 
overwashes possible.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
The Thanksgiving storm is still on track, with the bulk of the
rain and wind impacts most likely in the afternoon and evening. 

There remains some model uncertainty with regard to timing, so
the window for peak storm impacts remains roughly 10am thru the
overnight. However, this window in reality should be a bit
smaller, as the heavy rain and strong winds are cut short by the
dry slot blasting thru from the south. 

Although the exact magnitude of the winds is a bit uncertain,
confidence is high that strong winds will develop due to the 
strong pres gradient setting up. As a result, expanded the wind 
hazard to include an advisory for most of the area that was not
in the watch. The watch remains in effect. The GFS has strong 
winds aloft, and for the fcst mixed down 75% of the h95 winds. 
This brings 60 mph gusts to the watch area, and over 60 mph on 
the ocean. Drag from the heavy rainfall and poor llvl lapse 
rates would be the main limiting factors, but if confidence 
increases in the model, at least 80% of the h95 winds would not 
be unreasonable. In this scenario, peak gusts to 70 mph could be
possible on LI. 

The rainfall progs are fairly similar to previous runs, with
rain developing from the south thru the morning, and mdt-hvy
rain by aftn into the eve. Since the sys is moving roughly nwd
about 20kt, this should limit rainfall amounts as well as the 
overall flood threat. Regardless, deep lift to 40kft will 
support heavy rainfall rates as well as an isold elevated tstm. 
Would expect ponding on area roads and widespread minor flooding
of poor drainage areas. 

1-2 inches of rain with locally higher amounts to around 3
inches remains the fcst. 

The rain gets cut off by the dry slot in the eve, again the
timing will be refined as we get closer, with perhaps some
lingering light rain or dz under the residual stratus deck. 

The upr low and cold pool aloft come thru on Fri. This could
spark a few shwrs. Perhaps a wet snowflake could mix in across
the highest elevations with h85 down to -3C. 


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
With a recent full moon, astronomical tides remain rather high and 
many locations need less than a foot to reach minor coastal flood 
benchmarks with the AM high tides, but closer to 2 ft with the PM 
high tides.

Minor coastal flooding is expected with Wednesday morning's high 
tide for southern Nassau county communities, elsewhere localized 
minor coastal flooding or no coastal flooding.

A period of gale to storm force ENE winds will affect the region 
Thursday morning into Thursday Night btwn approaching low pressure 
and strong high pressure to the north. This will bring the 
likelihood for widespread moderate coastal flooding with the 
Thursday AM and PM high tides, with potential for major coastal 
flooding along the western Great South bay. Other areas of notes for 
significant impacts will be the Peconic Bay area with funneling of 
surge towards the Peconic River, and along W LI Sound shoreline with 
moderate water levels combined with high wave action. Surge up the 
tidally affected rivers (Hackensack, Hudson and Passaic will result 
in minor to moderate flooding as well.

The Thursday AM high tide is the higher high tide by at least 1 ft, 
but the peak surge will likely occur Thursday afternoon into 
evening, based on a multi-model mean of peak winds occurring Thu 
aft/eve. This may result in similar water levels for both tidal 
cycles for much of the area. The forecast has been leaned to a blend 
of 75th percentile of Stevens SFAS and NAEFS P-ETSS (good middle 
ground btwn ECWMF and GEFS PETSS) with deterministic ETSS/STOFS. The 
lean towards the higher end water level scenario to provide a bit of 
safety margin, if the timing of strongest winds is quicker than 
currently forecast and with expectation of winds increasing thru the 
time of high tide Thu AM.

For the Friday AM high tides, winds switch to the southwest. 
Potential for another round of moderate coastal flooding for the 
southern bays of LI and Queens, particularly for the eastern Great 
South Bay with potential seiching of water from west to east. 
Elsewhere, offshore flow should allow for water to drain out of
more open water location (LIS and NY/NJ Harbor) resulting in 
minor coastal flood impacts. 

For the oceanfront, breaking waves of 8 to 12 ft will result in 
widespread beach flooding and dune erosion during times of high 
tide. There is potential for localized overwashes, exacerbating 
flooding of roadways and vulnerable structures behind protective 
dunes. Along Western LI Sound and Twin Forks, breaking waves of 3 to 
6 ft will result in areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. 
Wave splashover will exacerbate flooding of roadways and vulnerable 
structures behind protective dunes and seawalls. There is potential 
for isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures as well.

Heavy rain coinciding with the Thursday evening high tides could 
exacerbate street flooding issues along the coast.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z WEDNESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
High pressure will be in control through Wednesday evening as it moves 
across to the north.

VFR conditions through Wednesday evening. MVFR ceilings develop for the 
city and southern coastal terminals towards and after 06z Thu. 

Winds N to NE around 10 kt or less overnight. Some outlying terminals
may briefly have light and variable winds. Winds shift to the ENE
Wednesday and settle in at 7 to 12 kt for much of the day.

     NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

No amendments expected.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z Thursday through Sunday... 

Late Wednesday night: VFR gives way to MVFR towards and after 06z. Winds
increase, especially towards the morning push.

Thanksgiving: IFR conditions in rain develop. E winds 15-25kt G30-40kt.
Peak gusts potentially higher. LLWS possible with 50+kt at 1000ft.

Friday: VFR and pockets of MVFR. W winds gusting to 25-35 kt. 

Saturday: MVFR possible with W winds gusting to 20-30 kt.

Sunday: VFR. SW winds 5-10 kt.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Winds and seas will subside a bit this eve, but waves are likely
to stay around 5 ft on most of the ocean thru tonight. As a
result, the SCA was expanded there thru the night. 

Seas begin to build again on Wed from the south, so a SCA may be
needed for all of the ocean. Winds are expected to remain blw
SCA lvls otherwise. 

Winds and seas become dangerous on Thanksgiving as low pres
impacts the waters. The Storm Watch remains in effect for gusts
aoa 50kt. Seas on the ocean are modeled to build to around 20ft
at the height of the storm in the late aftn and eve, with waves
on the Sound around 10ft. 

Conditions improve a little on Fri, but a SW gale is possible,
particularly ern waters. Winds down to SCA lvls on Sat, and
perhaps blw SCA lvls on Sun.
